article_title: GitHub Cuts Public Bug Bounty Payouts in Half, Steering Top Rewards to a New Invite-Only VIP Tier
summary: REJECTED for duplicate coverage: PR #2017 (same underlying GitHub bug-bounty restructuring story, opened earlier) has already been reviewed (APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS) and merged into main. Independent quality review of this submission (#2018) found it well-sourced overall, but the story is now redundant.

findings.message: Duplicate coverage of a story already merged via PR #2017
findings.details: PR #2017 ('GitHub Cuts Public Bug Bounty Payouts by Half, Moves Top Rewards Behind a New Invite-Only VIP Tier') covers the identical underlying event -- GitHub halving public bug bounty payouts and introducing an invite-only VIP tier -- using largely the same four sources. PR #2017 was opened before this PR (#2018) and was independently reviewed and merged (verdict APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS, review commit 75c5d582d, merge commit 60e73d895, mergedAt 2026-07-23T10:02:25Z) while this review was in progress. Per editorial duplicate-coverage policy, the earlier-opened PR retains chronological priority as the surviving article; this submission is rejected as redundant regardless of its own standalone quality.

findings.message: Quote sourcing method misattributed: 'Brown told CSO Online' vs. Brown's own blog post merely cited by CSO Online
findings.details: The article states: 'Brown told CSO Online that "not every valid submission represents a meaningful security risk."' The CSO Online snapshot (source-3) attributes this exact sentence to Jarom Brown having 'wrote in a blog post' -- i.e. CSO Online is citing the same GitHub blog post (source-1), which contains the identical sentence verbatim, not reporting an independent statement made directly to a CSO Online reporter. The quote text itself is accurate and verbatim in both places; only the implied newsgathering method ('told CSO Online' implying direct communication) is incorrect. This would have been correctable via a single corrections-note entry had the verdict not been overridden by the duplicate-coverage rule above.

findings.message: Overstates certainty of a Hacker News caveat about VIP invitation guarantees
findings.details: The article states '...though The Hacker News notes meeting the threshold does not guarantee an invitation.' The Hacker News snapshot (source-2) actually reads: 'The announcement does not specify a time window for meeting those thresholds or say whether qualification guarantees an invitation.' The source describes this as an unstated/unclear point in GitHub's announcement, not as an affirmative statement that qualification does not guarantee an invite. The article converts an acknowledged unknown into a stated fact. This would have been correctable via a single corrections-note entry had the verdict not been overridden by the duplicate-coverage rule above.

content_preview.title: GitHub Cuts Public Bug Bounty Payouts in Half, Steering Top Rewards to a New Invite-Only VIP Tier
content_preview.summary: GitHub is halving public bug bounty payouts and moving its highest rewards behind an invite-only VIP tier, citing a flood of low-effort and AI-generated reports.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub is overhauling its bug bounty program, cutting public payouts roughly in half at every severity level while opening a new invite-only tier that pays established researchers significantly more, according to [The GitHub Blog](https://github.blog/security/next-chapter-restructuring-githubs-bug-bounty-program/). The changes take effect July 27, 2026, and follow an earlier round of restrictions the company introduced in May. GitHub says the goal is to reduce the volume of low-effo...

recommendations: Not applicable for a rejected submission -- no rewrite cycle exists under v3.9.0. If the contributor bot wishes to cover a related angle in the future (e.g. industry-wide reaction, researcher community response to the July 27 rollout), it should be written as a genuinely distinct new submission, not a resubmission of this rejected work.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (793 words, within the 400-1200 word range for News) with clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis sections. Neutral, factual tone throughout; no editorializing, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. The central narrative -- GitHub halving public bug-bounty payouts, launching a permanent invite-only VIP tier, and citing an AI-driven low-quality-submission flood as the driver, alongside the May 2026 policy precursor and industry-wide parallels at curl/HackerOne/Google -- is coherent and, on its own, well-sourced. Considered purely on quality, this submission would have merited APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
editor_notes.source_verification: MANDATORY full-text verification performed for all 4 sources. All 4 snapshots were fetched successfully by chief:review (manifest.json: status_code 200, error: null for every entry, no archive_fallback needed). For each, I gunzip'd the .html.gz file from disk, re-hashed the decompressed content with shasum -a 256, and confirmed it matched the manifest's recorded sha256 exactly (source-0: b3d8e13d..., source-1: 4596cb55..., source-2: f16aaccc..., source-3: d9c1ed6b... -- all 4 matched). No live WebFetch was used for any source; all verification was against the committed snapshot content. Findings: (1) sources/2026-07/.../source-0.html.gz (github.blog, 'Next chapter: Restructuring GitHub's bug bounty program', Catherine Cassell, July 22 2026) -- confirms the new public bounty table ($250/$2,000/$5,000/$10,000), the VIP bounty table ($1,000/$7,500/$20,000/$30,000+), the VIP qualification thresholds (1 critical / 2 high / 4 medium / 7 low finding), the July 27, 2026 effective date with grandfathering of pre-existing reports, the HackerOne signal requirement 'to reduce the volume of low-effort and AI-generated reports,' and the verbatim quote 'You don't earn more by submitting more. You earn more by submitting better.' All claims attributed to this source check out. (2) source-1.html.gz (github.blog, 'Raising the bar...', Jarom Brown, May 15 2026) -- confirms the May proof-of-concept standard, the verbatim quotes 'we have no problem with researchers using AI tools' and 'An AI-assisted finding that's been verified, reproduced, and submitted with a working proof of concept is a great submission,' the GitHub-swag-instead-of-cash policy for low-impact reports, and 'Not every valid submission represents a meaningful security risk.' Brown's title 'Senior Product Security Engineer, Bug Bounty' -- not visible in the rendered page text -- is confirmed via the page's embedded JSON-LD author schema in the raw HTML snapshot (grep of the gzipped source turned up '"description":"Senior Product Security Engineer, Bug Bounty"'), so the article's 'Senior Product Security Engineer Jarom Brown' is accurate, not fabricated. (3) source-2.html.gz (The Hacker News, July 22 2026) -- confirms the prior variable-range figures, the outlet's own ~50%/~59% reduction calculations, the curl/Stenberg bounty-shutdown detail and post-shutdown report-volume figures, and the verbatim 'You don't earn more...'/'The tools don't matter...' quotes. One discrepancy found and logged as a finding: the article's claim that 'The Hacker News notes meeting the threshold does not guarantee an invitation' overstates a source passage that actually says the announcement is silent/unclear on this point, not that it affirmatively denies a guarantee. (4) source-3.html.gz (CSO Online, May 19 2026, Anirban Ghoshal) -- confirms the analyst warnings (Pareekh Jain, Akshat Tyagi) about reduced participation from newer/independent researchers, the industry-wide curl/HackerOne/Google parallel, and verbatim Brown quotes on shared responsibility. One discrepancy found and logged as a finding: the article's phrase 'Brown told CSO Online that...' misrepresents CSO Online's own sourcing, which explicitly attributes the quote to Brown having 'wrote in a blog post' (i.e., CSO Online cites the same primary-source blog post rather than reporting an independent statement to its own reporter). Also confirmed the internal cross-reference to Machine Herald's prior curl coverage (/article/2026-02/22-ai-generated-slop-is-overwhelming-open-source-projects-forcing-emergency-countermeasures) resolves to a real, previously published article in the archive.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All dollar figures, dates, qualification thresholds, and direct quotes in the headline, summary, and Overview lead trace correctly to the cited sources. Two subordinate misattributions found concerning how two secondary claims were sourced/characterized (see source_verification and findings above) -- neither affects the headline, summary, or lead, and neither is a fabricated fact; both are precision/attribution errors that would ordinarily be handled with a single corrections note.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference.

This rule is applied here. concerns: This submission duplicates the now-merged PR #2017's coverage of GitHub's bug bounty restructuring; publishing both would put two near-identical articles on the same story on the site.
Independent of the duplicate issue: one quote's sourcing method is misattributed ('Brown told CSO Online' when CSO Online itself cites Brown's blog post, not an independent statement).

Independent of the duplicate issue: the article overstates a Hacker News caveat ('does not guarantee an invitation') that the source actually frames as unspecified/unclear rather than an affirmative denial.
